name: Acmer S2 Pro 36W
tagline: Acmer S2 Pro mid-power: enclosed-optional 36W tier
tldr: Acmer S2 Pro 36W is the lower-power SKU on Acmer's S2 Pro line with rotary and IR bundle options. Compare to S2 Pro 48W before buying: often worth the step up.
mainObjective: Maximum cut speed and depth in the line: engraving remains strong at tuned speeds

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

cannot: 48W tier exists for more cut depth

pros: Built-in 30 L/min air pump: cutting setups need no separate compressor
Basic pack at $582 on Acmer's store (October 2026), about $178 below the 48W
Same 400 × 400 mm bed, 0.08 × 0.1 mm spot and 24,000 mm/min top engraving speed as the 48W
cons: Acmer publishes no cutting chart for the S2 Pro: our benchmark puts a 10 × 10 cm square in 3 mm basswood at ~7–12 min, slower than the 48W
Real fill speeds sit far below the 24,000 mm/min headline (~29–74 mm/s in our tests)
Rotary, camera and IR packs push the price to $686–1,227; the IR pack alone adds about $477
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 36W SKU on Acmer S2 Pro. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: On the 36W S2 Pro, run separate LightBurn profiles for photo fills versus basswood cuts. Push cut speed only after 10×10 cm test squares. Compare the 48W tier if evening batches still feel slow.

editorialDepth.advantages: Acmer S2 Pro 36W targets mixed engraving and wood-cutting weeks: fewer passes on basswood and dark acrylic than weaker SKUs in the same line.
editorialDepth.limitations: Wrong pick if you never engrave and only wanted the lowest price. Ultra-fine photo work can look better on an engraving-first SKU.

faq.question: How thick can the Acmer S2 Pro 36W cut?
faq.answer: Acmer does not publish per-thickness cutting figures for the S2 Pro. On our side, the profile lists basswood up to 8 mm (several passes at the upper end), and our 3 mm basswood test cuts a 10 × 10 cm square in ~7–12 min at 3–5 mm/s. Run a test grid on your own stock before quoting thick jobs.

faq.question: Which S2 Pro 36W pack makes sense?
faq.answer: Acmer's US prices in October 2026: Basic $582, Camera $686, Rotary $809, IR $1,059, All in One $1,227. The IR pack adds a 1064 nm module for marking bare metal, which the blue diode cannot do well; skip it if you only work wood, leather and dark acrylic.

faq.question: S2 Pro 36W or 48W: who should pick the 36W?
faq.answer: Hobbyists and engravers who cut occasionally. Both share the same bed, spot spec and built-in air pump; the 48W mainly shortens cut and fill times (our photo test: ~12–18 min vs ~14–22 min). The basic packs are about $178 apart ($582 vs $759.99).

standoutFeatures.title: Air assist built in
standoutFeatures.body: A 30 L/min air pump is integrated in the machine, so cleaner cuts and less charring need no extra purchase.

standoutFeatures.title: Cheaper entry to the S2 Pro
standoutFeatures.body: $582 basic pack in October 2026, about $178 less than the 48W for the same 400 × 400 mm frame.
